races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Distillation
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard recently and has placed form at this course; a genuine hold-up horse pushed into midfield on the map, meaning its chance relies on Athenian Spirit tiring and sufficient gaps opening, which the pace shape makes unlikely.

runners_data.name: Athenian Spirit
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who sets the entire tactical agenda here; naturally a prominent-to-hold-up type elevated to lead by default, but nine runs this season shows durability and five placed efforts over 7-8f on Standard suit course and distance.

runners_data.name: Hear The Drums
runners_data.note: Has a single win over 7f on Soft and fades in finish, a concern over this Fibresand mile; a true hold-up runner squeezed into midfield on the map, and the 51-day layoff with a flat recent form string — 91-087 — makes confidence hard to justify.

runners_data.name: Singarda
runners_data.note: Trainer Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood in form with two wins from 11 over 14 days; David Nolan is a positive booking and Singarda's five consecutive places at 8f suggest the trip is fine, with the move to Southwell from Goodwood the main unknown.

runners_data.name: Lady Fizz
runners_data.note: Lightly raced at just three runs and fades in the finish, which is a concern given this race looks like it will set up for staying power rather than a late burst; the apprentice claimer (7lb) could offset some of the OR disadvantage but the finishing tendency is a structural negative.

runners_data.name: Miss Mambo
runners_data.note: Gay Kelleway stable, placed at 8f on Soft and Standard, and blinkers fitted for today add an unknown dimension; this is her shortest AW trip at one mile, and she is a natural hold-up horse whose best chance comes if Athenian Spirit capitulates in the last furlong.

runners_data.name: Soda
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty in fair form with two wins from 20 over 14 days and Connor Beasley is an astute booking at Southwell; genuinely a hold-up horse shifted to midfield on the map, but three consecutive placed efforts over 6-7f on Good suggest this mile on Fibresand may be asking a question about stamina.

runners_data.name: Mist of Time
runners_data.note: William Knight has four winners from 19 runners over 14 days, a solid trainer angle; placed over 10f at Goodwood suggests stamina is not an issue, but the horse has been retreating through the handicap and its true running style means it needs more pace than this race is likely to serve up.

runners_data.name: Go Teejay
runners_data.note: Fitted with a hood today which is a headgear change worth noting; fades in finish and has a string of mid-to-high placings over 6-7f, and the step up to a mile on Fibresand looks like it could expose those finishing limitations further — apprentice claim (3lb) is modest compensation.

runners_data.name: Retro Rocket
runners_data.note: Martin Keighley has one winner from two runners over 14 days; limited form over 6-8f, all on Good or Standard, with a 33-day break and only three career runs meaning the form profile is thin — a genuine hold-up horse filling midfield on the map whose chance depends on circumstances the race is unlikely to create.

races.paceDynamic: Athenian Spirit is the lone confirmed pace-setter and will dictate from the front on a Standard Fibresand surface at Southwell, a flat one-mile track that typically rewards horses who can control proceedings without being harassed. With no genuine rival to press her early, she is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop, controlling the fractions and potentially stealing a march on the field as they fan out behind her. The bulk of this field — Distillation, Hear The Drums, Soda, Mist of Time, Go Teejay, and Retro Rocket — are all true hold-up types mapped to midfield purely because the race cannot accommodate them all at the rear; the field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the track shape can serve, meaning late closers will be fighting for the same ground from the same position. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in Athenian Spirit's slipstream and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, as the compressed hold-up group are likely to get in each other's way and receive an uncontested pace that is too measured to set up a winning late surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Athenian Spirit Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Athenian Spirit is allowed to dictate a measured, uncontested gallop throughout and the hold-up pack cannot close the gap.
scenarios.body: Athenian Spirit controls the pace from the front without a rival willing to challenge her, and the Standard surface rewards her rhythm-based front-running style over a flat mile; with the hold-up horses stuck in a cluster and racing out of their preferred roles, the ground between them and the leader proves too large to bridge late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Overwhelm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Athenian Spirit sets a faster-than-expected tempo that causes her to flatten out in the final furlong, opening the door for the hold-up cluster.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace would compress the race's final-furlong margin and give the truest hold-up types — Distillation and Miss Mambo — a chance to finish through beaten horses, though this scenario is dampened by the fact that most hold-up horses are racing out of role and likely to be too deep to deliver a telling blow.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracks Athenian Spirit at close quarters throughout and picks her off inside the final furlong as she tires.
scenarios.body: Singarda or Lady Fizz, without a natural front-running role but capable of racing prominently when given room, could track the pace and use a late sustained effort to overhaul Athenian Spirit if she runs out of petrol; Singarda's consistent finishing positions at Goodwood's stiffer test suggest stamina will not be an issue over this flat Southwell mile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners fight for position early, causing the race to fracture with several horses unable to settle and losing ground through interference.
scenarios.body: With seven horses genuinely preferring a hold-up role crammed into a midfield cluster, gaps may not materialise at the right moment and the race could fragment into sections, favouring a horse with enough positional flexibility to avoid trouble — Miss Mambo's recent headgear change adds a wildcard element in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Athenian Spirit could be dramatically underestimated in the betting market — as the only confirmed pace-setter in a field of hold-up types, she faces zero front-running pressure and any odds over evens may represent a structural advantage being underpriced.

The hold-up cluster of Distillation, Soda, Mist of Time, Go Teejay, and Retro Rocket are all racing out of role and mapped to midfield by necessity — watch for traffic problems and interference in the straight as they all seek the same late gaps simultaneously.

Hear The Drums returns after 51 days off and has a fading profile; if she is not fully tuned up, she could block the run of horses attempting to close from behind, making her a potential traffic hazard rather than a contender.

Singarda's trainer booking of David Nolan represents the strongest jockey-trainer combination on any non-front-running horse; watch to see if he positions her closer to Athenian Spirit than her OR suggests she should be, which would be a significant in-running signal.

Go Teejay's hood fitting is a first-time headgear change — horses wearing headgear for the first time at Southwell on the AW have a statistically variable response, and the apprentice jockey means any behavioural quirk in the stalls or early stages could compromise the hold-up group behind them.

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Ernie McCrew
runners_data.note: Consistent AW performer for J S Moore with 3 runs in 14 days suggesting stable confidence, but a natural hold-up horse who will be unable to secure a position as far back as he'd like in a field loaded with closers; form figures of 646745 offer no win in similar conditions and the style-fit discount applies.

runners_data.name: Here Comes Louie
runners_data.note: Roger Fell has used Kevin Stott, a solid operator, but the ⚠ fade tag is a significant concern over a mile — finishing record in similar going shows 0 wins and 0 places from comparable efforts, and a horse that fades in finishes is badly placed in a race where the front end is likely to control the pace clock.

runners_data.name: Alice's Influence
runners_data.note: J F Egan is the headline — a top-tier jockey on a filly with a tidy form string (1-2-3-4 placings from eight runs), and she's shown she can compete at this trip on Good ground; her natural style is hold-up but the crowded rear means she will drift further forward than ideal, which tempers confidence despite the quality of the ride.

runners_data.name: Gilleangirl
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa brings significant course and surface craft, but 121 days off the track is a notable fitness query; all three career runs have been at 7f on Southwell AW, so the step to a mile is an untested extension, and her best figure of 5th limits expectations even fresh.

runners_data.name: Starakova
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's filly carries solid claims — a Southwell 7f Standard win sits just three runs back, the step up to a mile looks well within range, and Harry Vigors' 5lb claim reduces the burden to a competitive weight; she is the natural tracker behind Gloriola and her prominent style is perfectly aligned with this race shape.

runners_data.name: Elashgar
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost have been active with this horse (3 runs in 14 days) and his form shows a win and two placings from five starts on Standard going at the minimum 5-6f trips; stepping sharply up to a mile is the primary concern — his best efforts have been over sprint distances, and a true mile on Fibresand tests whether that stamina extends.

runners_data.name: Gloriola
runners_data.note: Steph Hollinshead's filly is the race-shaper — confirmed sole front-runner, two recent Southwell AW placings at this exact trip and distance confirm track and surface affinity, and an uncontested lead with Clifford Lee on board gives her every chance of controlling the gallop from flag to finish; lowest OR in the field (49) means she carries least weight, compounding her tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Speckled Brown
runners_data.note: Andi Brown's yard has just one runner in 14 days and this horse arrives on a career-best form of 0-547; a true hold-up horse who, in a field full of closers, cannot get the race run to suit — the style-fit discount is meaningful, and 18 days between runs with no Southwell AW experience in the recent history adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Thomas Tallis
runners_data.note: John Mackie's gelding has been off 65 days, the longest absence in the field, and all four career runs have been on Southwell AW — familiar surface but form figures of 870-7 tell a difficult story; a natural hold-up type who is mapped forward out of necessity rather than choice, and his recent efforts suggest he is not competitive at this level even from a suitable position.

races.paceDynamic: Gloriola is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure — she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on Standard Fibresand over one mile at Southwell. With no rival willing or able to challenge her early, the tempo is likely to be honest but not punishing, meaning the lead is hers to control throughout without the need to expend energy repelling challengers. Starakova is the most naturally prominent of the remainder and should slot into second or third, tracking Gloriola's measured fractions in a race that could develop into a proper test of finishing quality rather than a sprint. This race shape heavily favours the lone front-runner and those racing prominently, as a controlled pace will not generate the late surge closers require. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Ernie McCrew, Alice's Influence, Speckled Brown and Thomas Tallis are all genuine hold-up horses but are mapped to midfield; of these, Alice's Influence (form and jockey quality) and Ernie McCrew are most likely to actually press into mid-division positions, but none will secure a truly prominent berth ahead of Starakova.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gloriola Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Gloriola is allowed to roll along in front at her own pace with no rival testing her early, the controlled fractions play directly to her strengths.
scenarios.body: Gloriola settles into a rhythm on the Fibresand and, with Clifford Lee timing her effort, she builds a lead that proves difficult to peg back — her recent 2nd and 3rd at Southwell over this trip confirm she handles the track well. Starakova, closest in rank, gets a dream stalking position and may be best of the rest, but Gloriola's solo advantage is the decisive factor.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Starakova tracks Gloriola close enough to strike two furlongs out and the pace proves just slow enough to allow a sustained challenge.
scenarios.body: Starakova's recent Southwell win over 7f on Standard going proves she handles the track, and stepping up to a mile with Harry Vigors (5lb claimer) reducing her burden gives her every chance of lasting home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If Gloriola sets a pace fast enough to create an opening-up race that allows genuine hold-up horses to close strongly from the rear.
scenarios.body: This scenario relies on Alice's Influence or Elashgar finding a clear run inside the final two furlongs, with J F Egan's experience and Alice's consistent form figures at this trip providing the ammunition — but Standard going at Southwell tends to be surface-speed-biased, limiting how far back late movers can come.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Gloriola goes off too fast early or fades sharply, compressing the field and creating a bunched finish.
scenarios.body: A compressed finish slightly benefits horses with the highest ratings — Gilleangirl and Elashgar would have the best chance of capitalising on chaos at the top of the straight — but this scenario requires an unusual collapse from the race's pace anchor and remains the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch Gloriola's early sectionals — if Clifford Lee allows her to stride on unchallenged from stall one, the race is effectively set; any hesitation in the gate or rival pressing in the first two furlongs could fundamentally alter the shape.

Starakova's draw and early positioning are crucial — if Harry Vigors slots her directly behind Gloriola within the first two furlongs, she becomes the primary danger horse; if traffic forces her wider or deeper, her chance diminishes sharply.

Alice's Influence is the redistribution horse to track — J F Egan will be looking to get a forward position that isn't naturally available to a hold-up type, and if she gets caught in traffic on the back of a cluttered midfield she may never get a clear run.

Elashgar's stamina for a mile is the single biggest unknown in the race — if connections have genuinely schooled him to see out the trip, his OR and recent strike-rate make him dangerous in the final furlong, but watch for signs of weakening from the two-furlong pole.

Here Comes Louie's fade warning combined with a 21-day break and poor sim-going record makes him one to dismiss unless you see early signs of an unusually fluent travelling position — monitor his market move (or absence of one) close to post.

races.name: Simon Davis Big 60th Birthday Bash Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ravishing Beauty
runners_data.note: Consistent recent form culminating in a course win over 8f on soft, and her prominent style suits sitting close to Hauteluce's honest tempo; 20 days between runs is comfortable for a five-year-old in form, and this Standard Fibresand surface is the key question given her soft-ground success.

runners_data.name: Hauteluce
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner who won over 10f on Standard AW last time and drops to 8f here; Ed Walker's yard is in excellent form at T14:10/36 and Ashley Lewis claims 3lb, making her the pace anchor around whom this entire race is built.

runners_data.name: Filly Eilish
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on Standard going and holds strong course form, but De Sousa will find herself shuffled into a midfield position because several prominent types contest that ground ahead of her — her true style is up with the pace and the style-fit discount applies.

runners_data.name: Zarinca
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Standard at Southwell and has a placed record on this surface, but steps up slightly in trip here; her prominent style gives her a chance to track the pace, though she drops in distance comfort zone compared to her best efforts.

runners_data.name: Dream Illusion
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose sim-going record on Standard is an excellent 3 wins from 15 trips, making her potentially the most likely of the closers to benefit if the pace collapses; Jason Hart rides and the 29-day break is not unusual for this trainer's horses.

runners_data.name: Kiss Me My Love
runners_data.note: Won most recently over this course and distance on Good ground, but her Standard AW record on similar going shows 0 wins from 4 attempts — that surface-specific blank is a clear concern despite her fine recent form; Joanna Mason and Roger Fell keep her fresh with just 8 days between runs.

runners_data.name: Kartini
runners_data.note: Her best recent effort was a second over 10f on Standard, suggesting she wants further than a mile; Simon Whitaker's yard is quiet at T14:0/7, and being pushed into a midfield slot she wouldn't naturally occupy further tempers expectations despite a reasonable placed record.

runners_data.name: Court Of Stars
runners_data.note: Luke Morris partner has two placed efforts over 7f on Standard and a win at the distance for Ollie Sangster's yard, which is in fair recent nick at T14:6/17; prominent in style, she is well positioned to track Hauteluce and poses a genuine each-way threat.

runners_data.name: Zermatt Star
runners_data.note: Has shown modest form overall with no Standard AW wins in recent outings, and her best finishes have come on Good or Heavier ground; David Nolan gives her every chance from a hold-up position but the evidence base on this surface is thin.

runners_data.name: Blue Celestial
runners_data.note: James Tate's three-year-old has strong placed form on Standard AW with six placings from 11 starts at sim-going, but her true hold-up style is displaced into midfield by the volume of closers in this field — the style-fit discount is meaningful and she is unlikely to get an ideal run.

runners_data.name: Gifts Differing
runners_data.note: Longest absence in the field at 54 days and a consistent back-marker who has yet to win on Standard or any surface; the lowest OR in the field at 57 and a style-fit penalty from being mapped out of her natural position make this a tough assignment for Jonny Peate.

races.paceDynamic: Hauteluce is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm on Standard Fibresand at Southwell over a mile. The pace will be steady-to-honest rather than pressured, creating a single-file procession where the leader controls the tempo from the outset and is never forced into a burning early split. Ravishing Beauty and Court Of Stars are the next-most-natural prominent racers and will track close behind, meaning the race likely strings out relatively early through the long Southwell back straight. This shape strongly favours horses with tactical speed who can sit within two or three lengths of the leader and produce a sustained run from the home turn — deep closers will face a stern test if Hauteluce is allowed to steal a decisive march. Crucially, Kartini, Filly Eilish, and Blue Celestial are all genuine prominent or hold-up types who cannot get their natural positions in this field, and among the true prominent runners, Hauteluce and Ravishing Beauty are best placed to actually secure early cover.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hauteluce Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hauteluce is allowed to stride clear and set a measured, sustainable gallop that suits her front-running style throughout.
scenarios.body: Hauteluce controls the tempo entirely without pressure, conserving enough energy to kick again in the straight and resist challengers who have to make up ground from behind; the honest Standard going at Southwell rewards a horse in control of its own race and punishes those running on from too far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Collide Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ravishing Beauty or Court Of Stars travel smoothly just off Hauteluce and produce a sustained challenge entering the home straight.
scenarios.body: The front-running tempo proves just quick enough to stretch the hold-up runners, and a prominent stalker lands the decisive blow inside the final furlong; Ravishing Beauty's course-and-distance win on similar going and Court Of Stars' consistent placing record make them both legitimate threats in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than it appears and Hauteluce's uncontested lead flatters to deceive, setting up a stronger-than-expected run for the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Dream Illusion and Kiss Me My Love, the two most legitimate rear-of-field types, would benefit if front-runners tie each other up or Hauteluce overpaces herself in isolation; Kiss Me My Love's recent win and Dream Illusion's good record on this surface make them the likeliest beneficiaries of a late collapse.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types — Kartini, Filly Eilish — push forward and create unexpected crowding and a faster early tempo than anticipated.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace scrambles the shape and opens the door for a fresher horse sitting just off the unruly bunch to pounce; however this outcome is materially discounted because Kartini, Filly Eilish, and Blue Celestial are already flagged as racing out of their natural position and their reduced style-fit lowers the probability of this shape materialising.

watchPoints.text: Hauteluce — if she bowls along unchallenged and Ashley Lewis finds a comfortable rhythm, she is the race-shaper and her uncontested lead could prove unassailable; watch whether any runner is brave enough to press her in the early stages.

Ravishing Beauty — her Southwell course win and prominent style place her ideally to attack Hauteluce in the straight, but her Standard AW form (1 win from 15 sim-going runs) requires scrutiny before taking that step forward at face value.

Kiss Me My Love — recent winner and freshest horse in the field, but her AW Standard record of 0 wins from 4 creates a genuine flag; if she fails to handle the surface switch she could be found out despite strong recent turf form.

Redistributed trio (Kartini, Filly Eilish, Blue Celestial) — all three will find themselves in a more congested midfield than their natural style demands; watch for traffic issues on the home turn if they attempt to improve from their unnatural positions.

Court Of Stars — quietly consistent with two wins and four places on Standard, sits just off the pace naturally, and Luke Morris's track knowledge at Southwell could make her an overlooked each-way runner if Hauteluce is collared late.

races.name: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Baarberini
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with one run to her name — a third over 7f on Standard Fibresand — giving her directly relevant going experience, but James Horton's stable is out of form at 0/12 over 14 days and she steps up to a mile for the first time, needing a strong enough pace to release her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Bullrider
runners_data.note: Lightly raced sort who has shown ability on both Standard and Good ground, but George Boughey's yard is in excellent form at 7/28 and Jack Callan knows the horse after a recent run 10 days ago; unknown in terms of running style assignment, he may find a prominent position here if he shows natural early speed.

runners_data.name: Phantom Knight
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Andrew Balding — a yard firing at 9/50 over 14 days — so going preference and trip suitability are completely unknown; Callum Hutchinson takes the ride and the horse must be treated as a genuine wildcard whose natural racing style will only become apparent once the stalls open.

runners_data.name: Astral Crown
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners this hold-up operator whose only run was a fifth over 7f on Good ground; although shown in midfield on the map, its true inclination is to race from the rear, and in a race where pace is controlled by Hoosthat alone, getting into a winning position from off the gallop will be the challenge — the style-fit discount applies here.

runners_data.name: Kodiac City
runners_data.note: Another first-time-out runner from Richard Hughes's yard, with Kevin Stott aboard and no form data available whatsoever; until this horse races, going suitability, trip preference, and natural style are entirely speculative, making it one to monitor in the early stages to see where it settles.

runners_data.name: Quest For Glory
runners_data.note: The one genuine prominent-style runner likely to push forward and make it competitive up front; Georgina Nicholls has a small but focused string and the horse has two runs over this same course and surface at 7f, providing the most directly relevant course-and-distance experience in the field, which is a tangible asset stepping up to a mile.

runners_data.name: Vinery
runners_data.note: Ran second over 6f on Good ground before a disappointing sixth at 7f, also on Good; David Nolan takes the ride for Oliver Greenall and Josh Guerriero whose yard has sent only one winner from nine runners recently, and the hold-up style means Vinery is reliant on the pace being strong enough to set up a late challenge, which is not guaranteed here.

runners_data.name: Hoosthat
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter who finished eighth on his only start over 7f on Good ground and carries a fades-in-finish flag; William Muir and Chris Grassick saddle him off a 59-day break, and while his role shaping this race as an uncontested leader is clear, his tendency to weaken late means his chance of lasting home over a mile against improving rivals is genuinely uncertain.

races.paceDynamic: Hoosthat is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 8-runner novice stakes over Southwell's flat fibresand mile, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Jason Hart can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop without any pressure from rivals. Quest For Glory is the one prominent-style runner who may push forward and track Hoosthat, but there is no horse capable of forcing a truly contested pace, meaning the early fractions should be modest and the race is likely to develop into a slowly-run affair until the tempo quickens in the straight. The hold-up brigade — Baarberini, Astral Crown, and Vinery — will be doing their best work late, but a conservative pace from the front may blunt their finishing kick before they can close the gap. Astral Crown has been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are more hold-up types in this field than the rear of the race can accommodate; in reality it is a genuine back-marker and will likely race further back than its mapped position suggests. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a sustainable, controlled pace — strongly favours horses who can sit handy and quicken from a prominent position rather than those who rely on a truly strong pace to fuel a late challenge from off it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hoosthat Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hoosthat leads without any serious early pressure and Jason Hart dictates a measured pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Hoosthat takes the field along at a comfortable gallop, controlling the fractions from gate to straight and kicking clear before hold-up horses can find their stride; horses tracking in second and third are best placed to capitalise if Hoosthat's stamina wanes late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Quest For Glory pushes up to genuinely challenge Hoosthat for the lead, injecting more pace than anticipated and setting up a contested front-running battle.
scenarios.body: The increased tempo burns off Hoosthat earlier than expected and the race opens up for those sitting just off the pace in third to fifth positions; horses with tactical speed and the ability to quicken from a handy berth will be best equipped to sweep through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough through the middle part of the race to genuinely suit horses coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Hold-up runners get the fast-enough gallop they need to unleash a sustained late run down the straight, and the front two tire within the final furlong; this scenario is discounted because Astral Crown and Vinery are true back-markers who may not get the truly strong pace they require.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutants Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If one or both of the unexposed first-time runners — Phantom Knight or Kodiac City — show the ability to quickly slot into a prominent position and deliver a sharp performance on debut.
scenarios.body: A lightly raced or first-time-out runner with natural pace finds the race developing at a tempo that suits a horse switching on quickly, and the form horses fail to handle the Southwell surface or trip; this scenario carries low probability given the limited data on both runners.

watchPoints.text: Hoosthat's fades-in-finish flag is the central risk in this race — if Jason Hart sets too slow a pace to conserve his stamina, the field bunches and late movers get a soft lead to aim at, transforming the shape entirely.

Phantom Knight and Kodiac City are both first-time-out runners whose natural pace and settling pattern are unknown — either could disrupt the projected pace map by pushing forward aggressively from the gates, forcing Hoosthat into a contested lead earlier than expected.

Astral Crown's redistribution away from the rear means Tudhope may find himself further back than ideal and with less pace ahead to chase down in the straight; watch whether he can secure a position that gives him any realistic chance.

Quest For Glory's two runs over this exact course and surface at 7f give her the strongest course form credentials in the race — monitor whether Harry Vigors pushes forward from the gate to track Hoosthat, because if she does, it changes the race from a solo-lead shape to a two-horse pace contest.

The overall form level in this race is modest outside the OR=120 horses, and several runners are lightly raced or unraced — any market move on Phantom Knight or Kodiac City in the final minutes before the off should be treated as significant stable information.

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Hectic
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey runner off a 55-day absence dropping back to 6f on familiar Standard ground, wearing hood; his best Southwell form (4th twice) came from a true hold-up position but this field's abundance of closers means he cannot get to the back — a genuine back-runner squeezed into midfield traffic, which is the worst possible scenario for his style.|

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen partnership for Iain Jardine who is in decent form (4/24 over 14 days), and this horse has two placed efforts over 6f at Southwell on Standard — by some distance the best course-and-distance profile in the field; a natural hold-up type who at least has a tactical record suggesting he can produce a late run when the race sets up.|

runners_data.name: Moostar
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride for James Owen (12/57 over 14 days, active yard) and the horse carries headgear; his last run was 20 days ago and he has five placed efforts from 15 on similar going but no win — pushed out of his preferred rear position by the congestion of hold-up horses, he may be forced to race closer than ideal.|

runners_data.name: Daytona Lady
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr runner who is highly experienced at Southwell (13 starts on this going surface, one win and six places) and is the most battle-hardened horse in the field at this track; James Sullivan rides and the horse naturally likes to close from off the pace — the sheer number of hold-up rivals makes finding a clear run the critical challenge, though her course record is a genuine asset.|

runners_data.name: Court Drive
runners_data.note: Gay Kelleway yard (quiet, 0/2 over 14 days) and the horse ran well last time with a win over 6f on Soft and has placed on this Standard surface before; blinkers fitted and a natural hold-up runner who has won on this going combination — like several rivals, finding room in a closing-packed field is the obstacle rather than any ability concern.|

runners_data.name: Ottawa
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope is a significant positive booking and this horse has won over 6f at Southwell on Standard (form figure 1 in recent string), but he has not run for 173 days — the layoff is the key flag; a hold-up type whose profile suits the course perfectly if fit enough, though fitness off such a gap on a track that rewards horses in peak condition is a material risk.|

runners_data.name: Showtime Mahomes
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer runner also returning after a lengthy break (163 days) and the horse has won on this exact course and going (1/6f/STA); a hold-up type who has placed only once in 15 starts on similar ground since that win, the long absence mirroring Ottawa's fitness question, and the lack of recent momentum tempers the appeal of that course win.|

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Condor
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby's runner with James Doyle booked — an immediate upgrade in class of jockey — who wears a visor and was placed over 6f on Good last time; the sole front-runner in the field, and the combination of a professional front-riding jockey, an uncontested lead, and a flat Fibresand track makes his tactical position the most privileged in the race.|

runners_data.name: Cairdeas
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley handler who is quiet (0/21 over 14 days) and this horse has only placed three times in 15 outings on similar going with no wins; David Nolan rides and the form string shows a pair of seconds but no win on Standard, and the limited Southwell course form (two 12th-place finishes here) is a significant concern on a track that rewards familiarity.|

runners_data.name: Miraculous
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby yard (3/84 over 14 days) and David Allan in the saddle for a horse whose recent form is exclusively on Good or Soft ground — zero wins and only one place from three starts on similar Standard going in the sim-going profile is a clear flag; a hold-up horse who has not won on this surface type and faces the same traffic problems as every other closer in this field.|

races.paceDynamic: Ziggy's Condor is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 6f Southwell handicap and, with no other genuine pace horse to challenge him from the break, he is likely to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than being dragged into a headlong duel. James Doyle's booking on a horse wearing a visor over OR 70 adds significant tactical weight — a professional ride from the front on a flat, standard-ground Fibresand track where leaders can be notoriously hard to peg back. The field is loaded with hold-up horses — Hectic, Moostar, Daytona Lady, Court Drive, Ottawa, and Showtime Mahomes are all natural hold-up types who have been pushed into midfield on the map because the rear of the race is over-subscribed; several of them will not get the deep closing position they want. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile: with one uncontested leader likely to set a controlled tempo and a host of closers crowding the wide outside late, Ziggy's Condor's opportunity to control from the front and a small number of genuinely prominent or tactically flexible horses represent the most advantaged profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ziggy's Condor Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ziggy's Condor jumps cleanly and is allowed to dictate a comfortable tempo with no rival willing to take him on.
scenarios.body: He settles in front, sets fractions that suit himself, and Doyle times the kickback through the final two furlongs to hold the closers at bay on a track that consistently rewards front-rank performers at this trip. This shape punishes the over-populated hold-up division, who need a true strong pace to close into — and they are unlikely to get it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Splits Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is marginally stronger than expected and one of the true closers finds a clear passage from midfield into the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A genuine hold-up type who avoids the traffic jams in a field crammed with similar runners threads through the pack as the leader tires in the closing stages, getting up close home. Pickersgill, with strong Southwell form (two placed efforts at this course and trip on Standard), and Daytona Lady, the most course-experienced hold-up type in the field, are the likeliest beneficiaries if this shape materialises.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Grinds Through
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is honest enough to string the field out and one of the redistributed hold-up horses manages to track closer than their natural style and produce a sustained run.
scenarios.body: A horse forced to race prominently against their instinct — such as Moostar or Court Drive — finds themselves in a fortuitous position and stays on strongly as others disappoint from true hold-up positions at the back. This is a low-probability shape because the horses best placed to win it are not naturally suited to the position they would need to occupy.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Mover Pounces Early
scenarios.trigger: If Ziggy's Condor is slow away or becomes uncharacteristically unsettled and a prominent racer moves into the lead to force a genuine test.
scenarios.body: The pace becomes genuinely contested, the fractions increase, and a horse with tactical versatility who can travel in the first three without fighting for position picks up the pieces late. This is the least likely shape given Doyle's experience, the horse's clear edge in early pace, and the absence of any other confirmed front-runner in the field.

watchPoints.text: Ziggy's Condor — watch the first two furlongs to confirm he jumps cleanly and secures the lead unchallenged; if any rival moves to press him before halfway the entire pace dynamic flips and closers become significantly more dangerous.

Ottawa — Daniel Tudhope's booking on a course winner at this trip is compelling, but 173 days off the track is a serious fitness question at Southwell where peak condition matters; watch market moves in the final hour for clues about stable confidence.

Pickersgill — with two Southwell placed efforts on Standard over 6f this is the closest thing to a form-proven closer in the field; watch his position at the two-furlong pole — if he has a clear run he is the most dangerous hold-up horse to Ziggy's Condor.

Daytona Lady — 13 runs on this surface type make her the most course-experienced runner, but James Sullivan will need to find a gap in a field where six or seven horses all want to be doing the same thing in the final furlong; watch for traffic at the two-furlong marker.

Showtime Mahomes and Ottawa both return from breaks exceeding 160 days — if either shows above-expected market support late, treat as a significant stable confidence signal worth noting before the off.

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Fierce
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Paul Midgley with a solid sim-going record (8/15 at Standard, 1W 3P); steps up to 6f from his recent 5f runs which is a potential positive, though his last Southwell 6f run was a 7th-place finish to note.

runners_data.name: Baba Reza
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 8-year-old has placed twice at 6f Southwell Standard this season, but at his age and with a 31-day absence, his actual racing position will be further back than the map suggests — he's a genuine closer who needs things to happen in front of him, and this race shape provides little help.

runners_data.name: Jesse Luc
runners_data.note: Boasts the most relevant course-and-distance profile in the field with 14 of 15 runs on Standard going and multiple placed efforts over 6f at Southwell; his natural instinct to race from off the pace is constrained by the field's makeup, though his familiarity with this exact track-surface-distance combination keeps him in the picture.

runners_data.name: Sarafina Mshairi
runners_data.note: The key pace influence — Edward Smyth-Osbourne's 4-year-old won over this C&D on Standard going and returns after 49 days with a 3lb claimer booked; the layoff is a small fitness query, but her front-running profile is uniquely advantaged by the absence of any rival pace.

runners_data.name: Camera Shy
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' 4-year-old wears a tongue-tie and has been off 93 days — the significant absence is the primary concern; a natural hold-up horse who won over 7f on Standard, he faces the double challenge of racing off a slower pace and returning from a long break.

runners_data.name: Fan Mail
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard is in good form (T14: 3/84) and Fan Mail wears a hood, racing prominently off the pace; recent Southwell AW form is limited but the 6f trip suits, and a prominent position in a steady-tempo race is exactly the scenario this profile needs.

runners_data.name: Beattie Is Back
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's 7-year-old has posted three consecutive 15th-place finishes on Good ground recently, and his two simulated-going placed efforts came at Standard but the strike rate is modest; Ethan Tindall (5lb claimer) takes off useful weight but the recent form is deeply uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Dorney Lake
runners_data.note: The most authentic closer in the race — Liam Bailey's 5-year-old won over 6f at Southwell on Good going and arrives on a 13-day turnaround in good fitness; his Standard-going record is limited (6/15) but the course form is genuine, and he represents the sharpest late threat if the shape opens up.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Jenny
runners_data.note: Back after 73 days for Steph Hollinshead, but the form profile is excellent — 1-2-2 in her last three starts including a Southwell 6f win on Standard; a prominent-racing type who thrives on this course and surface combination, the absence is the only note of caution.

races.paceDynamic: Sarafina Mshairi is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 6f handicap on Standard Fibresand at Southwell, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, she should dictate from the gates at a controlled, sustainable tempo. Fan Mail and Spirit Of Jenny will press forward into prominent positions just off the pace, giving the race a modest early tempo that is unlikely to produce a truly punishing gallop. This shape — a single, uncontested pace-setter at manageable fractions — strongly favours horses racing in the first three or four, as the leader will not be run into the ground and closers will find it hard to generate enough momentum off a steady pace to close the gap in the final furlong. Baba Reza, Jesse Luc, and Camera Shy are genuine hold-up types who cannot all operate from their natural rear position in a small field with limited traffic to thread through, meaning their redistribution to midfield on the map reflects race reality rather than preference, and their effectiveness as closers is compromised.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sarafina Mshairi Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sarafina Mshairi jumps cleanly, sets an uncontested lead, and the pace stays measured throughout.
scenarios.body: Sarafina Mshairi dictates every yard at a comfortable tempo, turning Southwell's straight six into a solo time trial that rewards her front-running profile; the lack of genuine pace pressure means her 6f course win at Standard conditions translates directly here. Horses racing prominently off a slow-to-moderate pace receive the most benefit, as any late challenge is blunted by the absence of a searching gallop to bridge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind Out
scenarios.trigger: If Fan Mail or Spirit Of Jenny track Sarafina Mshairi closely enough to wear her down and pounce approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: One of the two prominent closers overhauling a slightly weakening Sarafina Mshairi is plausible given both have placed form in this grade over 6f on suitable going, and Spirit Of Jenny's recent 1-2-2 run of form gives her a live chance if she travels smoothly in second. Fan Mail carries proven Southwell AW course form and Easterby's yard has been active, making a forward-tracking winner very achievable in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final 2f, creating a gap, and one of the redistributed hold-up types produces a late burst.
scenarios.body: Jesse Luc has the strongest simulated-going record in the field (14/15 at Standard) and carries course-relevant form, giving him the best profile among the displaced hold-up horses if the scenario demands a late finish; however, all three redistributed types are racing out of their natural rear position, which structurally limits their ability to produce the sustained late run this shape requires. Dorney Lake, a genuine hold-up operator whose recent Southwell form includes a course win, is the more authentic closer in the field and represents the most credible threat in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Sarafina Mshairi is pressed harder than expected early and ties up in the final furlong, gifting the race to a late flourish.
scenarios.body: Should an unexpected speed duel develop or Sarafina Mshairi simply fail to see out the trip after her layoff, the race opens up for any horse with residual energy; Dorney Lake (course winner, LR 13d) and Fierce (strong Standard-going record) would be best placed to capitalise on a messy finish. This scenario is low probability given the confirmed absence of a rival front-runner, but the 49-day absence of Sarafina Mshairi introduces a small fitness unknown.

watchPoints.text: Sarafina Mshairi's 49-day absence is the critical variable — if she shows any sign of greenness or fitness loss leaving the stalls, the entire pace dynamic changes and the race becomes far more competitive for the prominent pair.

Spirit Of Jenny returns after 73 days having won at this exact course and distance on Standard going — the layoff is the only thing stopping her being marked as a stand-out, so watch market support to gauge trainer confidence.

Camera Shy's 93-day absence is the longest in the field — Michael Dods' horses can reappear fresh, but a hold-up horse needing race fitness in a moderate-tempo race is a combination that rarely produces a winning return.

Jesse Luc and Baba Reza are both mapped to midfield but are genuine hold-up horses — if they are forced to race closer than usual due to field compression, their finishing kick may arrive earlier than ideal and exhaust before the line.

Fan Mail's hood and prominent style places her directly in the sweet spot of this pace shape; David Allan is an experienced hand around Southwell and the stable's recent strike rate (T14: 3/84) indicates the yard is firing — straightforward tactical positioning to monitor.

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Astro King
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for Kubler, returning after 55 days and stepping back to Fibresand; his last five runs are all on turf at Goodwood/Haydock and he has no recent AW form to draw on, making this a significant surface switch at OR 97.

runners_data.name: King's Code
runners_data.note: David Evans's six-year-old carries a hood and is in cracking recent nick — won over 10f at Goodwood nine days ago — and his course-and-distance equivalent form (9/15, three wins, four places on similar going) makes him one of the best-credentialled runners here; natural prominent style suits this race shape.

runners_data.name: Ultrasoul
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old arrives on a hat-trick of wins, all on soft or standard going, and his AW standard form of 3W from 9 runs is exceptionally strong; C Y Ho rides and the drop back after a 54-day break looks no bar given his versatility, with a prominent pitch suiting the anticipated race shape perfectly.

runners_data.name: Let's Dream
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's five-year-old won twice on good ground but has never threatened on AW standard going in five tries; his natural inclination is to race prominently, but with so many similar types in this field he is likely to find himself shuffled into a midfield role that does not suit — the combination of surface doubt and positional compromise is a significant double negative.

runners_data.name: Port Of London
runners_data.note: Gosden's four-year-old holds two wins on Fibresand standard (including over 12f here) and the course form is genuine, but 227 days off the track is a serious concern; he races with a hood and, though his heart is in the front rank, the crowded prominent berths mean he cannot easily access that position — returning from a very long layoff in a race where he cannot settle where he wants is a tricky ask.

runners_data.name: Say What You See
runners_data.note: Luke Morris partners this four-year-old who won on Fibresand standard over 10f and 12f in her last two STA runs, giving her real course-going credentials; she races with a hood, is 55 days fresh, and her hold-up style means she is not directly inconvenienced by the redistribution — one of the few genuine late-running types with proven AW form.

runners_data.name: Jimmy Speaking
runners_data.note: De Sousa rides a horse who has won on both STA and SOF going and whose natural game is to race up with the pace; with three other prominent types competing for position, he is squeezed into a midfield slot that blunts his effectiveness — the step up to 1m3f from recent 1m trips is also an untested stamina question.

runners_data.name: Cloth Of Gold
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old ran a solid 2nd over 10f on Fibresand standard last time and has the requisite course form (1W, 4P in nine STA runs); he races hold-up and finished 4th over 11f at Goodwood 20 days ago — the AW surface suits and Andrew Mullen claims no allowance, so he needs to hit form on his merits.

runners_data.name: Per Contra
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old is busy (19 days since last run), wears a hood, and his best AW standard form (3 places from 15 runs, one win) suggests consistent rather than explosive — OR 80 is competitive but his recent form string of 034804 shows no win since that one STA success and he lacks the pattern to suggest a dramatic improvement here.

runners_data.name: Virtual Rock
runners_data.note: John Butler's seven-year-old carries a massive 138lbs off OR 104 and has been absent 741 days — an enormous layoff that makes any assessment of current wellbeing speculative; he won over 16f on good going and has no AW standard form at all in the sim-going record, so this is a significant ask on return from injury.

runners_data.name: Spinning Wheel
runners_data.note: The Crisfords' four-year-old is the only confirmed front-runner in the field and faces no genuine pace challenge, giving Oisin Orr a simple tactical choice; placed at both 13f and 14f on soft/good to soft, this standard Fibresand trip is slightly different ground, and his last run was 61 days ago — if his fitness level is right, the race is his to lose.

runners_data.name: El Burhan
runners_data.note: George Boughey's four-year-old wears a tongue-tie and returns after 90 days; his one win at 10f on soft going and a 5th on Fibresand standard suggest modest AW credentials (0W from 10 sim-going runs), and the prominent style means he competes for a position that is already crowded — the layoff and limited course-going form make him hard to recommend at face value.

runners_data.name: French Duke
runners_data.note: James Doyle rides for Al Jehani, and French Duke won over 12f on good going last year but has run six times since on good ground with modest returns (one win, no places in last five); Fibresand standard is an entirely new surface (0W, 0P in 13 sim-going runs) and that blank record on the artificial strip is a glaring red flag despite the quality of the pilot.

races.paceDynamic: Spinning Wheel is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should coast to the front from the off and control a measured, sustainable gallop over this 1m3f Fibresand trip at Southwell. King's Code, Ultrasoul, El Burhan, French Duke, and Virtual Rock will fill the prominent berths behind, creating a compact early order rather than a contested pace — the tempo will be genuine but not pressured, favouring those who can track and pounce rather than those waiting deepest. The field holds more front-running or prominent types than the race shape can accommodate, with Let's Dream, Port Of London, and Jimmy Speaking — all true prominent racers — unable to secure their natural position and likely shuffled into a midfield they do not naturally inhabit, which meaningfully discounts their prospects. This shape strongly favours the horse who sits second or third on the bridle tracking Spinning Wheel's controlled pace and has the class and stamina to assert from two furlongs out, making prominent-to-midfield closers with proven Southwell or standard-going form the key beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Spinning Wheel Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Spinning Wheel leads cleanly at a sustainable clip and the prominent pack track without disruption, allowing a true test of class and stamina.
scenarios.body: Spinning Wheel sets a controlled, uncontested pace and the race develops into a battle between those immediately behind him, with the winner most likely the horse who has tracked closest and has the turn-of-foot to collar the leader inside the final furlong.
winners: Runners with proven standard-going form who can sit just off the pace — notably Ultrasoul and King's Code — are the primary beneficiaries of this most likely shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Strike Early
scenarios.trigger: If King's Code or Ultrasoul press Spinning Wheel from the outset, injecting slightly more pace and ensuring any hold-up runner cannot reel in the leaders in the straight.
scenarios.body: A mildly contested early pace still produces a leader-dominated finish, but the winner comes from the group of two or three immediately behind Spinning Wheel rather than the leader himself.
winners: Horses with strong standard-going records sitting handy — Ultrasoul and Port Of London — are well-placed if pace quickens slightly
though Port Of London's long absence adds risk.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is faster than it appears and those out in front tire in the final two furlongs, opening the door for genuine hold-up runners to sweep past.
scenarios.body: Astro King, Cloth Of Gold, and Per Contra are the true rear-of-field types who would benefit, though none show compelling Southwell or AW standard-going form to inspire confidence.
winners: The scenario is limited in probability because the three redistributed prominent types — Let's Dream
Port Of London — are not natural hold-up horses and are unlikely to produce true late finishes from these positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Redistribution
scenarios.trigger: If the displaced prominent runners — Let's Dream, Jimmy Speaking — contest for positions they cannot naturally hold, causing a messy, erratic early order.
scenarios.body: Positional friction in the first half-mile disrupts Spinning Wheel's rhythm and bunches the field, creating a lottery finish where luck in running plays a large part.
winners: This is the least likely scenario given the clear pace hierarchy
horses with tactical versatility and strong current form like Ultrasoul are best placed to adapt.

watchPoints.text: Virtual Rock's 741-day absence is an extreme risk — watch how he moves in the parade ring and whether Connor Beasley is instructed to hunt a position early or nurse him round, as either outcome signals the trainer's confidence in his fitness.

Port Of London is 227 days off the track and will likely be unable to access his natural prominent position due to the crowded pace map — if he is visibly keen or unbalanced leaving the stalls, his chance evaporates quickly.

King's Code and Ultrasoul are likely to be within three lengths of Spinning Wheel throughout; if either jockey decides to press for the lead entering the back straight, the pace dynamic changes materially and the late runners' prospects improve sharply.

Let's Dream and Jimmy Speaking, both natural front-runners displaced into midfield, could become restless or over-race from unfamiliar positions — watch the first two furlongs for any signs of positional scrimmaging that disrupts Spinning Wheel's intended solo lead.

Say What You See's two AW standard wins suggest she handles this surface well, and her hold-up style means she is unaffected by the redistribution — if Luke Morris gets a clean passage on the inner turning into the straight, she could prove a significant each-way factor in Scenario C.

runners_data.name: Meet Me In Meraki
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type for David Evans and J F Egan, with 2W3P on similar going in the form book; recent finishing positions of 3rd and 2nd at Goodwood show residual form, but dropping back from 12f to this 11f equivalent and racing mid-pack rather than from the rear limits the late-run potential here.

runners_data.name: Golspie
runners_data.note: Patrick Morris runner who has hit the frame consistently at 10-12f on standard going (12/15 sim-going with three placed efforts), but is a genuine hold-up horse whose true position at the back of the field will instead be a midfield slot, diluting the finishing run this horse depends upon.

runners_data.name: It's Only Fun
runners_data.note: Jonny Peate partners this Sara Ender-trained 4yo who has won at 11f on standard AW (1W1P sim-going) and recorded a recent Goodwood second over 12f; a closer by nature, the crowded hold-up group means it races in a midfield role it isn't ideally suited to, though the trainer's 0/6 in the 14-day window is a minor dampener.

runners_data.name: Luan
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back on standard going over 10-12f for Nick Scholfield and Daniel Muscutt (2W2P sim-going), making this one of the more potent hold-up profiles in the race; displaced into midfield from its preferred rear position by the glut of closers, though the horse's recent winning form over this course-and-distance type gives it more upside than most in the same situation.

runners_data.name: Dingwall
runners_data.note: David Allan rides this Tim Easterby 5yo who is the only genuine prominent-style runner aside from Titainium, meaning it is almost certain to secure its natural stalking position just off the leader; Goodwood form shows consistent placed efforts (2W8P overall) and the trip is fine, making this the horse most likely to mount a late challenge to the leader.

runners_data.name: Blackwaterfoot
runners_data.note: A Charlie Pike-trained 5yo returning after 57 days off — the longest absence in the field — with headgear noted (p) and only 6/8 sim-going runs producing no wins or places on standard; a true hold-up type shuffled into midfield with a weak recent form line (6180-0) and no visible trainer momentum (0/8 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Distinction
runners_data.note: John Mackie's 8yo veteran is a natural closer who will find itself in mid-division rather than hunting from the back; a win at 8f soft and a place at 8f soft shows best form is likely on a different surface/trip combination, and the sim-going record (4/15, 1W1P) doesn't scream confidence at Southwell.

runners_data.name: Cavalry Call
runners_data.note: Patrick Morris double-header with Golspie, this 5yo (hg:p) has a deeply unencouraging recent string (77-870) and only one Southwell win in the record at 10f; a genuine hold-up horse operating out of its ideal position, and the sim-going record (5/15, 1W2P) combined with the weakest form figures in the field makes this a significant concern.

runners_data.name: Into Combat
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's 4yo is flagged as fading in finishes — a meaningful handicap for any closer — and the trainer is in strong form (10/29 in 14 days) which is the best angle here; however, the horse's all-weather record is thin (3/8 sim-going, 0W0P) and the fade-in-finish flag means even a perfect run from midfield may not convert.

runners_data.name: Sisterandbrother
runners_data.note: Jason Hart partners this Joey Ramsden-trained 8yo who has won twice at 12f on Good and once at 12f on Standard (1W4P sim-going); a hold-up type that has produced big days at Goodwood over 12f, and the step to 11f here on Fibresand is the marginal trip concern, though it is one of the stronger form profiles among the closer brigade.

runners_data.name: Junkyard Dog
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 4yo (hg:v) has spent recent starts at 17-20f on soft, making this 11f standard surface assignment a very different proposition; only 1/15 sim-going appearances and a 0W0P record on standard going is a stark flag, though the recent 2nd at 11f Goodwood shows some residual ability at a shorter trip.

runners_data.name: Titainium
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's 5yo is the only confirmed front-runner in the race and Oliver Stammers takes the ride; won over 10f at Goodwood and has prior form at 14f, suggesting this 11f trip is within range, but the sim-going record (1/15, 0W0P) on standard surfaces is weak — the tactical advantage of uncontested lead control is the primary case, not raw form.

runners_data.name: Norflondonforever
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves partners this Faye Bramley-trained 5yo who won over 8f on Standard (1W2P sim-going, 4/8) and has been placed at Southwell before; a natural hold-up type who will sit deeper than ideal in a race full of closers, and the recent form line (41-800) shows a horse that has gone off the boil since a promising spring outing.

races.paceDynamic: Titainium is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 1m3f Southwell handicap and, with no other genuine pace challenger to push them along, is set to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over the standard Fibresand. Dingwall is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely track Titainium in second, meaning the pace shape is essentially set by one horse — a recipe for a steadily-run race that compresses the field and makes it hard to come from the clouds. The overwhelming majority of this field are natural hold-up types, but the redistribution note is critical: Golspie, It's Only Fun, Luan, Blackwaterfoot, Distinction, Cavalry Call, Into Combat, and others are all genuine closers who will be squeezed into midfield positions they don't want, reducing their effectiveness as true late finishers. This race shape — a lone leader controlling a steady tempo with a compressed midfield — firmly favours the prominent and front-running profile, with Titainium and Dingwall best placed tactically, though any runner able to travel close to the pace will hold the positional advantage over those forced wide or boxed in midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Titainium Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Titainium is allowed to bowl along at an uncontested, honest-but-not-punishing gallop and the midfield pack cannot unwind a telling challenge from their compressed positions.
scenarios.body: Titainium dictates every fraction from the front, building a lead that the hold-up pack — many racing out of their natural role — simply cannot reel in over 1m3f at Southwell; the track's turning configuration rewards those in front early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Clear Late
scenarios.trigger: If Titainium and Dingwall draw away from the squeezed midfield pack in the straight, rewarding the two horses that actually secured a forward position.
scenarios.body: With the hold-up contingent unable to produce their typical sweeping late run because they're stuck in a bunched midfield, the front two pull clear; Dingwall's proven Southwell course form gives them a real threat to Titainium late on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: One Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to bring the field back to the closers and one of the redistributed hold-up horses finds a gap from midfield.
scenarios.body: A truly honest gallop set by Titainium would allow a horse like Luan or Sisterandbrother — who have won at this trip on standard Fibresand — to produce a finishing run, but the slow-tempo risk makes this scenario less reliable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Chaotically
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses mid-race, the field concertinas, and a late flourish from an unexposed or lightly-raced type catches everyone out.
scenarios.body: Compressed mid-race traffic creates interference entering the straight, allowing a runner like Junkyard Dog or Norflondonforever to steal through late; this depends on circumstances outside normal tactical play and is an outlier shape.

watchPoints.text: Titainium has a clear tactical advantage as the sole uncontested front-runner — watch whether Oliver Stammers elects to dictate from the front or sits off the pace, as the decision in the first furlong will set the shape of the entire race.

Dingwall is the only horse in the field with a natural prominent style to track Titainium — watch whether David Allan places the horse directly behind the leader at the break, as this is likely the most important piece of positional real estate in the race.

With eight or more hold-up types genuinely compressed into midfield, watch for traffic trouble entering Southwell's home bend — a crowded, concertina-effect turn could eliminate several fancied closers before the straight is even reached.

Luan's two recent wins on standard going over 10-12f make it the most dangerous of the redistributed closers — watch whether Daniel Muscutt manages to find a prominent enough pitch from the midfield pack to launch a meaningful run, given the horse is operating out of its preferred rear position.

Into Combat's fade-in-finish flag combined with Sir Mark Prescott's 10/29 trainer form over 14 days creates an interesting contradictory angle — watch whether the fitting headgear or track conditions produce a different finishing effort, though the flag is worth noting for those expecting a late surge.
